correctness.rationale: The theorem treats all integers m,n>=2 and every labeled code. Selected rook vertices each with exactly one selected neighbor form disjoint K2 components in L(K_m,n), hence vertex-disjoint selected P3 edge paths in K_m,n. Distinct empty original vertices cause empty or duplicate signatures, so at most one unused; an unmatched vertex forces the other-side-centered orientation. For spanning configurations, m=2a+b,n=a+2b and selecting centers/leaf pairings gives m!n!/(2^(a+b)a!b!); unmatched case gives n!/2^m or m!/2^n. Sufficiency follows from distinct component incidence-set signatures. Independently checked direct open-neighborhood signatures over 366416 candidate subsets of nine boards, matching all nine formula counts. This finite test corroborates but does not replace the all-size combinatorial proof.
